key_insight: WPG-MoE improves user-level depression detection by using weak semantic priors to route each user to the most suitable expert instead of relying on one monolithic classifier.
clinical_relevance: This could support earlier, more nuanced social-media-based depression screening, especially for users who do not clearly self-disclose symptoms.
method: Uses a shared large language model backbone with a dense mixture-of-experts design.
Learns user-level weak priors from structured LLM-extracted evidence to guide expert routing during training.
Applies a learning-using-privileged-information setup so inference keeps only PHQ-9 template screening and the deployable backbone.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on Chinese and English datasets, where WPG-MoE outperformed strong baselines and showed interpretable routing behavior.
watch_item: Performance and interpretability may depend on the quality of the privileged LLM-extracted evidence, and the approach still requires careful validation before real-world screening use.
paper_title: WPG-MoE: Weak-Prior-Guided Dense Mixture-of-Experts for User-Level Social Media Depression Detection
